As Apple previously pledged, Tim Cook will continue to be involved in Apple's global government relations work after stepping down as CEO, and this week he met with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Details below.

Tim Cook discusses EU Kids Act with European Commission President

Apple previously announced that Tim Cook would step down as CEO on September 1, with the company stating:

Since taking on the role of Executive Chairman, Cook has kept that promise.

A few days ago, Bloomberg reported that Cook would attend the state dinner hosted at the White House on Thursday evening, September 24, for Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Just days before that report was published, Cook had posted on X that he hosted Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the Apple campus.

After the meeting, Albanese reportedly revealed that Cook described Australia's social media restrictions on children as "world-leading".

Yesterday, Cook continued his tour of meetings with world leaders, sitting down with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

von der Leyen posted on X that the two discussed the EU Kids Act and "agreed on the importance of protecting children's privacy, safety and well-being".

The proposed legislation would restrict minors' use of social media across the European Union and require platforms to provide stronger safeguards for younger users.

The meeting took place in Manhattan, where world leaders are gathering for the United Nations General Assembly.

It remains unclear whether Cook will or has met with other world leaders, but if such meetings occur, news is likely to surface soon from the relevant officials.
